verdict.rationale: Lithic documents a dedicated sandbox, described as 'a safe environment mirroring production' for running cards, transactions, and webhooks end-to-end. It also has sandbox-only endpoints for simulating acquirer-originated transaction events, which supports testing without touching production. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that the MCP/AI-editor tooling can be pointed at the sandbox (vs. 'live API requests'), documented isolation mechanics such as separate sandbox keys or base URL, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: A safe environment mirroring production — run cards, transactions, and webhooks end-to-end.
The sandbox environment has additional endpoints to simulate transaction events originating from a merchant acquirer.
Simulate an authorization request from the payment network as if it came from a merchant acquirer.
Create a virtual card and assign it to a test account
